display_title: Everything is Crab: The Animal Evolution Roguelite

reviews.text: 孩子们，谁懂玩一半发现这游戏没有存档功能的救赎感，退出去就算你这一把白玩了
刚上手还是新奇的，玩久了体验过于重复，视听效果单一，单局时长基本固定，还不能中途退出，玩着太疲惫了； 血量或速度达标前容错低，一不留神容易被秒，也还是蛮有挫败感的； 键鼠和手柄控制好像也不能改，可玩性有待提升，内容也不够丰富……虽然很愿意支持，但还是压一下评分吧
没有局外成长，越玩越坐牢，这点不改不行
好玩，希望多多优化，后期玩法有点匮乏，但是还是不错的，多出点生物就更完美了
局外成长几乎为0，难度越高游戏体验越差，没有什么新机制只是单纯的调整数值以加大难度，刚开始可能还觉得新鲜，后面只觉得重复乏味。运气成分极大，就算你好不容易运气好点，刚成长起来了，还没开始爽就结束了，作为肉鸽游戏这对吗？每一局都是没有存档的无法保存，要么你就打完这一整局，要么就别开始，这也很影响游戏体验。不知道之后会不会改进，如果能改得更好这游戏确实值得推荐。（我要借助神秘力量了）
胃大无需多言

这游戏就是一坨狗屎，压力19怎么打？18是刷了二十多遍运气好才过，19刷初始都刷了四十多遍，只打到1次最终boss，结果还过不了。怪物加攻速的体验和之前完全不是一回事，苍蝇还好说，伪果鼠恶心的要死，主角前期移速和蛆一样，只能跑，只要反打就会被打到完全躲不了。制作组真的有玩过高难吗？垃圾游戏 这游戏玩了十个小时，打到了压力13，浅谈下游玩感受和为什么打差评 [h3] 一. 难度做的烂 [/h3] 游戏低难度还算简单有趣，高难度完全是一坨屎。 1.低难度下，容错非常高，无论玩什么流派都能轻松通关，也能让人试玩不同的流派。 2.打到压力12，主角的性能就和蛆一样，我重开刷初始搞了十几把才通关。这时候敌人加血加成长速度掉的食物少；而主角没有几个加移动速度的技能，还有移速递减，升级所需经验增加一堆debuff；boss还有攻击修正啥的。玩着太坐牢了 3.技能稀有度，感觉高难度下技能稀有度好低，重开的十几把大部分是1级升级连个紫色都没有，增加重开次数 [h3] 二. 怪物做的烂 [/h3] 1.在主角移动速度非常低的时候，有的怪物还是跑的非常快，尤其是首领贼貂，都打残了就开始跑，完全追不上 2.做的最恶心的就是龟形兽，如果ai逃跑，你完全无法对它造成伤害，我玩到现在遇到太多回这种情况，你想和它打它却逃跑。真的傻逼的要死 3.帽子鸟，比龟形兽差点，但也差不到那里去。进洞穴就完全不出来。尤其是首领被差一点打死，进洞里等半天也不出来。 4.怪物种类太少，总共只有19种，玩到后面重复性太高 [h3] 三. 技能 [/h3] 1.技能加移动速度的太少，除了boss掉的技能，普通技能就没几个加移速的 2.当库存里攻击或移动技能时，会一直给你刷这个攻击技能的进化 3.就像前面提到那样，高难度下体感低等级的稀有度都很低，哪怕刷新也基本是绿色和蓝色 4.技能的专精太少，大部分技能都只是单纯给数值，没有特色。玩多了没啥意思 5.蘑菇生成的外观做的是真恶心，最有性价比的技能，基本上是看到必选，结果还做成绿色的痘痘 6.群体类的技能不好用，魅惑的怪物ai太蠢，啥用都没有。加成给的数值也好低，而且不小心打死魅惑的怪物还会掉属性，纯屎 [h3] 四.游戏内容 [/h3] 这是我觉得这游戏做的非常烂的一个地方，技能和怪物种类本来就少，低难度想玩无尽模式居然要去打到压力10.虽然我打到压力10比较轻松，但其他人呢？ 还有一些基因啥的也逼着人去打高难，有几个人能打到压力20？估计制作组的人都不见得有几个能做到 挑战也是，压力不够就没法玩 [h3] 五.总结 [/h3] 游戏就前几把好玩，高难度是屎，内容相当少和试玩差不多，而且通过难度来限制玩家游玩内容。总之我不推荐购买。

初见着实很惊艳，相较demo时期更加丰富：奇形怪状的进化效果，独特的升级机制，多样化的主动/被动技能连携……这些在低压力下确实给人带来了相当程度的乐趣，毋论是从玩法上还是从实际演出效果上都体现了“动物进化”这一主题。然而除了解锁基因外目前[b]几乎为0的局外成长[/b]，使得上述体验在高难度下沦为了一场糟糕的噩梦。 高压力难度下，己方的初始性能很差（移速加成惩罚，成长速度惩罚，敌人对己方有额外伤害加成），击败敌人后掉落的食物（用来提升角色等级的经验道具）和基因（升级时提升所选技能的稀有度）明显减少，且升级时所获得的技能稀有度较低难度而言明显降低。在此前提下，与敌人拉近距离变成了一件非常困难的事情（再加上本就极少的位移技能），反过来说一旦在发育期被大量敌人黏上，游走缠斗或者脱身也会变得相当艰难，更何况还存在着如裤豹和喷吐鱼等具有高机动性能的敌人。[b]大部分前期低难度可用的构筑乃至和平路线在高压力下将变得不再有效[/b]（比如躲躲藏藏和平发育靠社交来控制敌人代打的流派），这直接削弱了对于类rogue游戏而言颇为重要的多样化路线。最重要的是，[b]局外成长的缺位导致了玩家唯一应对高难度的方式只有不断提升个人的操作水平[/b]，但它的尴尬之处在于本作在动作交互方面的设计又不像常规的动作游戏那样有着多样化的处理方式（以及与此相应的个人提升空间）。 在技能构筑设计上，除却前面提及的位移技能极少（且不易选取），目前几乎所有的攻击性技能除了吸血/破甲/中毒/远近程等效果、与物理/技能/生命值的关联和攻击范围不一外，就没有其他的技能特性了。到了中后期，各项效果的区分往往不如数值上的堆叠造成的效果来得直观，这很容易使得不同的进化路线所体现出的特征只集中在玩家操控的角色外观上的改变和数值的改变上。此外，敌人种类和攻击方式的稀少和高重复度的地图也容易使得玩家在反复游玩中感到乏味。 就目前游戏版本的阶段而言，《万物皆可蟹：动物进化》确实有着非常新颖的理念和概念呈现，值得为此给本作一个好评。但由于上述原因，倘若制作组只是止步于此的话，那么它所取得的这些创新毫无疑问将会被它的短板所淹没。希望后续更新能补上目前的短板，不断打磨至更加完善的状态吧。

首先我得承认，这款游戏对我而言十分新颖，也带给我不少的惊喜，就像《孢子》一样通过各种奇异的进化线路来构建出属于自己的进化物种，并取得最后的胜利，这些体验带给我的新鲜感和成就感都不少，但是这款游戏的不足之处实在有点瑕已掩瑜。第一点就是游戏数值不平衡，肉食路线和草食路线的难度完全不同，成为一位食物链顶端的流程就是顺水推舟，每一步都能有收获，每一步都能让自己变得更强，而且这种反馈十分快速且有效，但是当一位被捕食者的体验就很糟糕了，怪物漫长的仇恨时间，对于草食玩家而言过高的伤害和移速，同时因为难以主动捕猎所以进化也十分缓慢，往往跟不上怪物进化的步伐，并且本应该成为草食玩家的选择的食物--蘑菇则凭借毒性让玩家前期稀少的血量无以为继，而草食路线提供的毒性抗性对于其所需要的实在太少。这些缺点让游戏原本应该拥有的复杂且有趣的流程变得单一。就我个人而言我觉得草食玩法实在是太艰难了，我自己来修改的话可能会增加一些像反刍的劣化版本技能来增强过渡能力，比如我可能会增加在草地上可以缓慢增加基因点数的技能，或者可以啃食树木或仙人掌一类的技能，毕竟作为食草动物可以吃草应该是一件理所应当的事情。第二点就是局外成长太少，由于难度的增加是毫不留情的，所以玩家感受到的压力也是水涨船高的，这一点也让游戏数值不平衡的问题更加突出，毕竟不同的线路强度差异太大，而过高的压力则逼迫玩家不得不选择那些更加强大的玩法。第三点就是游戏的内容不足，敌人的类型是固定的，但数量却太少，难以支撑起如生物进化这种宏大题材的丰富度，玩到后面看到相同的敌人和boss让玩家很容易感到厌倦。同时游戏内的技能也不足，没有提供出模拟生物进化本该有的复杂多样、百花齐放的图景，而且所有的额外机制似乎都不如数值提升来的有效，毒液玩法想要成功获胜所花费的时间与精力和只点增大体型与增加伤害的玩法相比显得效率低下，这一点实在有些让人失望。 总而言之，我希望制作组能在之后的修改中针对玩家遇到的问题进行修正，同时增添新的游戏内容，让这一潜力十足的游戏能真正的获得成功而非昙花一现。 First of all, I have to admit that this game is very novel to me and has brought me many surprises. Just like "Spore", it constructs its own evolutionary species through various strange evolutionary paths and achieves the final victory. These experiences have brought me a lot of freshness and sense of achievement, but the shortcomings of this game are a bit hidden. The first point is that the game values are unbalanced. The difficulty of the carnivorous route and the herbivorous route is completely different. Becoming a top player in the food chain is a process of following the flow of the river, where each step can yield rewards and make oneself stronger. This feedback is very fast and effective, but the experience of being preyed upon is terrible. Monsters have a long hatred time, high damage and movement speed for herbivorous players, and evolution is also very slow because they are difficult to actively hunt. Mushrooms, which should have been the food of choice for herbivorous players, rely on their toxicity to make the player's scarce health in the early stage unsustainable. The toxicity resistance provided by the herbivorous route is also very slow for them. What is needed is really too little. These drawbacks make the complex and interesting process that games should have become monotonous. Personally, I think the herbivorous gameplay is too difficult. If I modify it myself, I may add some degraded version skills like rumination to enhance transition ability. For example, I may add skills that can slowly increase gene points on grass, or skills that can gnaw on trees or cacti. After all, as a herbivore, it is only natural to be able to eat grass. The second point is that there is too little growth outside the game. As the difficulty increases mercilessly, the pressure felt by players also increases, which makes the problem of imbalanced game values more prominent. After all, the strength of different routes varies greatly, and excessive pressure forces players to choose more powerful gameplay. The third point is that the content of the game is insufficient. The types of enemies are fixed, but the number is too small to support the richness of grand themes such as biological evolution. Seeing the same enemies and bosses after playing can easily make players feel bored. At the same time, the skills in the game are also insufficient, and it does not provide the complex, diverse, and diverse scenes that simulate biological evolution should have. Moreover, all the additional mechanisms seem to be less effective than numerical enhancements. Compared with the gameplay of only increasing body size and damage, the time and energy required to successfully win the Venom gameplay is inefficient, which is somewhat disappointing. In summary, I hope that the production team can make corrections to the problems encountered by players in future modifications, while adding new game content, so that this potential game can truly achieve success rather than being a flash in the pan.

开局一只史莱姆，蠕动到该局结束依旧市区。 前几个小时满分五分，越往后面玩三分甚至更低。 低难度确实爽，但高难真不是人打的。 类幸存者肉鸽没有局外成长就算了。 高难直接不给再生，意味着开局受伤就要蠕动找回血食物或者找兴趣点看有没有再生，再没有就有摁着鼻子拿那绿色+1再生。 怪群也是，喜欢我超雄🐝群和伪🍎虫群吗，一窝蜂冲上来一口咬个半死，蠕动逃跑速度还慢没人家快，你恼羞成怒想打死它要三次甚至四次攻击，但是自己说的身板脆得跟纸一样。 走位不慎被围攻更是不得不品的一环，boss没怪群难有懂得吗？就算蠕动到最后一个boss了，你要面对一个带aoe，会召小怪甚至头目还有场地伤害的惊天boss,没构筑好就暴毙。 最高难度是压力20，但是你想打无尽还得通压力10，不给爽的来了。 怪也基本同质化，就一个怪进化两三次，史莱姆能进化得千奇百怪，怪固定提升反而更怪了。 现在基本就恩找驼峰和囊颊，想玩普攻流前期要拿攻击方式，要拿回血，要拿体型（跟攻击距离挂钩），但是体型打了又不好打boss.要拿想玩的套路组件，想试试别的套路又不一定刷组件。玩闪避流上限75％，血量低点也容易暴毙。想吃蘑菇随到个致命又是当场升天。 打不过高难去试试挑战，然后发现挑战在除了限制之外还绑压力（难度），容错巨低，我打那个达尔文挑战暴毙了15次，我真赤不下去了😭
谁懂当你好不容易急头白脸的打过进阶10解锁无尽，满心欢喜的跑到宝宝难度打完蟹海怪才发现不能在低于难度10开启无尽模式的救赎感吗

高难度设计的很同质化，和低难度的区别只是追你的超雄怪物变成数值怪了，而且你的回复数值差了很多。 单纯是要求你前期更胡而已。 而且本游戏设计上可能进化方向更贴近现实，但是整体玩法因此变得非常无聊：高难度完全不可能和野生动物正面对抗，甚至扛两下就可能要死了，更何况本游戏非常非常难见到加速度的天赋。一整把都在逃命就算了，甚至后面还有迅速提速的怪物尝试秒杀你。 就，这种体验作为一个rougelike完全不合格，极度小概率胡的情况下，胡了还很不爽。而且局外成长几乎不存在，只有解锁选项和开局的天赋而已。压力5以上的游玩全是些堆砌时间碰运气的重复刷取工作。 所以目前感受到的游戏内容就是：一直在和第一局类似的关卡和体验，不断重复的游玩后续数值完全崩溃但是机制毫无变化的版本。也就是几乎在前面10局通关以内耗尽新鲜感。
没有局外天赋不是很认可，然后不知道为什么局内要单独列举出吞噬速度这种没什么用的鸡肋天赋，甚至跳过天赋选项都能算是一种基因选项就很无语，如果后续更新还要搞压力玩家的平衡性改动，那这游戏还是别买吧，但目前还是给个好评，毕竟还是有潜力的

1、掉落物品太少，可以掉落怪物的器官 2、吞噬进化的目的太弱，基本就是一直吃东西吃东西。进化出来的动物与游戏里的怪联系太弱，怪是怪，你是你，两者没有关联。 3、好不容易得到的突变点，只能用来刷新物品，太肤浅了吧 4、这个游戏十分适合创意工坊 另外做个补充，这个游戏不是动物进化，它只是把武器做了个贴图放到了身上罢了，和以撒里面物品特效一样。真正的进化是蚂蚁不进化是杀不死大象的，应该把怪做个区分，以此突出进化的效果，而不是用个嘴什么都能咬死。一点自己对进化的理解。

大就是好！大就是高伤害！大就是坚硬！ 小就是好！小就是打不着！小就是滑溜！ 大就是好！大就是打穿防住！大就是肉蛋葱鸡！ 小就是好！小就是上下闪躲辗转腾挪！小就是山里灵活的狗！ 压力16之后局外成长不足和平衡稀烂开始严重影响游戏体验 当你能够通关的选择只有某几种时 这一款rouge游戏实际上就是失败的 你的游戏经历就从咦这一套打法也好玩哇这样居然也能通关变成了这次又没拿到大体型又没拿到蟹钳算了下一局 当过程变成目的 这款游戏就失去了游玩的价值

5/10，没给差评纯价格良心，过了新鲜感后体验是越玩越差，说几个毒点，怪会逃跑这个设定纯恶心，虽然很多肉鸽也会有这种设计，但人家不缺移速啊，这游戏开局机动性真的是跟他建模一样，没腿的，加移速的基本都是红卡，而且吃一两张照样追不上怪，弥补了很多人没当过蛆的遗憾。 bd构筑这块也做得不咋地，作为肉鸽最重要的一环，设计的真是各种何意味，像回血10秒一跳，使得这个属性就纯废物，“增加回血食物掉率”一张卡就让所有古法回血成为笑话；缩小闪避流也是纯废物，因为75%的闪避上限非常容易叠，体型还影响攻击和进食距离，得不偿失；武器间差距也是巨大，真不知道这个投石是何意味，手感稀碎还就两发弹容，加上仓鼠嘴也就六发，伤害拉跨还要一发发手瞄蓄力，武器多样性设计是创造新流派或渡前期用的，不是拿来凑数的。 还有难度方面后期就是各种数值碾压，讲真的搞那么多难度还不如学学土豆兄弟、痛苦殿堂，多设计几套流派玩法。无尽模式也是凑数，无尽跟普通局应该是两种不同类型的挑战，是拿来挑战每个流派的上限的，而不是拿来助眠的。

生活不如意可以玩，钻地洞不出来的鸟，抢食物跑的巨快的狗，只能抓攻击空隙的龟，时不时晕你一下的爬虫和吐口水的鱼，故意恶心你的粪怪这片大地上遍地都是，打赢了几块肉打输了直接重开。想当和平主义者捡泔水不是给你刷一堆移速快伤害怪仇恨锁定你就是给你刷两个毒蘑菇毒死自己，没有能力杀星星拿突变就算了交的动物朋友都是智障，不会护主乱跑乱打，被boss一巴掌群死。所有动物都是移速快有机制的大粪，而你，我的朋友，你只是一条在地上慢慢爬的蛆

将《孢子》的多样化生物创造乐趣与俯视角肉鸽战斗的玩法相结合，便组合成了本作独立游戏《万物皆可蟹：动物进化》。本作游戏最令人印象深刻的并非其生硬而累手的战斗，而是生物通过多种不同的进化带来的视觉奇特感受。玩家操控的主角从一只毫无尊严的软体生物史莱姆起步，通过吞噬食物提升等级从而产生变异不断进化，逐步拼接出拥有蝎尾、蝶翼、象鼻与蟹钳的奇特形体。这种万物皆可拼接的高自由度，让每一局游戏都变成了一场不可预测的生物实验。并且游戏还拥有多个环境地形与生态，让玩家拥有多个生存途径，提供给玩家较为自由的环境和体验。 [h1]通过进食成长与进化[/h1] 在进入游戏之后，玩家将扮演一只毫无尊严的软体生物史莱姆，最初只拥有较小的体型和很弱的攻击方式，其他几乎一无所有。在本作游戏中，玩家可以通过战斗的方式击败敌人，获取食物，也可以扮演一名拾荒者，拾取掉落的食物。总之玩家需要通过吞噬食物来获得成长，提升等级，从而获得一次进化的机会。游戏的核心部分并非战斗，而是生存。游戏中的玩家主动攻击也并非传统的类幸存者游戏的自动攻击，而是需要玩家主动按键，因此也可以衍生出一些完全不战斗的进化方式，可以坐山观虎斗，在相应的区域看其他的生物之间进行捕食和战斗，然后冲上去吞噬接着逃跑。甚至全程不参与战斗通关还能完成一个成就。 玩家的每次进化都会随机抽取三个分支，能够改变基础属性值或是新的攻击方式，并且进化还有颜色的区分，稀有度越高的进化可以获得更高的数据。生物的进化还没有伴随着外观的改变，可以让原本毫无尊严的史莱姆长出外壳，进化出双腿，长出翅膀，拥有象鼻或是鹰嘴。值得注意的是，游戏中虽然玩家可以拥有多种攻击技能，包括近战远程和技能攻击等，但是每次只能装备两种主动攻击的方式，其他的只能作为后备力量或是为主动攻击方式提供属性成长和被动效果。游戏的进化种类丰富，并且可以通过完成游戏内成就来解锁更多的进化方向，不断解锁新的内容，为玩家带来前期丰富的自由度和游戏内容体验。 [h1]缺少局外成长元素[/h1] 游戏目前是不包含局外成长的，玩家通关一个难度就会解锁更高难度的关卡，但是敌人的强度增强，而玩家初始依然是一只手无寸铁的毫无尊严的史莱姆。即便通过完成成就解锁了一大堆可以进化的方向。但是仍然需要玩家在每一局中经历痛苦的前期，吞噬提升等级才有机会体验这些新的内容。游戏目前包含的内容比较有限，也期待游戏未来可以更新出更加丰富的成长方向和内容，进一步扩充可玩性。 [code]欢迎来到[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/43883840/] Hello, World！[/url]，畅所欲言，探索游戏的无限可能。[/code]

Gets boring really quickly, I think the demo overplayed it's hand, its a solid 80% of the game. The main problem is the pressures (difficulties) actively make things worse. It basically turns the speedy game into a slow one where enemy density plays far too much of a factor in how the game progresses. The aesthetics are very charming, with good audio and visual polish, the idea is great, and its initially interesting. Overall there is far too little variety, in evolutions, attacks, movement abilities, enemies, overall builds and bosses, after about 5 hours you've seen everything the game has to offer and then some, after that its all repetition. Even the challenges don't change much, they are minor difficulty modifiers, or they zoom in the screen, just basic small modifiers that don't substantially change how the game is played, there just isn't enough to remix to notice a difference. The game needs about double its content, beyond its charming veneer there is little substance, its just doing the same thing with minor variations. Ultimately you are moving around, hitting things with a similar sized attack, using one of the very similar dodges while your numbers go up slightly, sure your character might change visually, but your mechanical inputs and how you think of the game stays almost exactly the same. If this was one of the first bullet heavens you could give it a pass, but the fact that basically all its competitors have more depth is not a good sign. The fact they are already talking about a paid expansion while the game is so barebones is NOT a good sign. Its a very affordable game, but honestly Steam is too competitive, you can get some of the greatest indie games of all time bursting with content for a similar price, it just needs more, a lot more, so much so that it will be multiple months if not years before I can recommend this game.

1 of Many (see comments) The game has a great concept that really clicked with me when I found out about it. Having the "Evolution" choices visually represented on your character is incredibly fun! I do wish I could sometimes choose how the odd Evo looks on the character. For example, the "Wings" "Branching Evolution" will look different depending on your current affinity values, and is chosen based on your highest affinity (from what I can surmise); this is extremely cool, obviously, though I do wish I could choose the "Imposing" affinity wing style usually (and/or ban whichever is the butterfly wings, I think "Gregarious" affinity but I could be wrong). I also think this game concept could be turned into an incredible long form survival game (even a 3d one a la Spore but better), *cough* hint, hint *cough*. It's got legs, even when Darwin doesn't! ...moving on... While I really love & enjoy the game, I cannot recommend it in its current state. Don't get me wrong, you could buy it, have fun, and enjoy your time playing; play long enough though and you'll come to notice its flaws and potentially, as I have, become frustrated with them. Currently there are too many issues that make the game feel non-fun and unfairly weighted for me to recommend the game. There's also a lack of variety in builds that becomes noticeable after awhile. Don't get me wrong there is some variety but not much. Addressing All Bosses: · "Aquaconda" gets bullied unless you have taken no Branching Evolutions with "Terrain Adaption". · "Clawdia" can overwhelm you with her children and webs, as they don't seem to have a reasonable spawn limit, causing you to be unable to move. Her children also do not drop food on death. Which makes this fight feel exceedingly unfair as she gets unlimited backup and you get stuck in place with nary a heal. · "Crabtuar" is a similar story to Shellephant, without extra speed the only way to effectively survive is to kite her around a tree. If you don't, her horn attack will most assuredly hit you as the timeframe to avoid it is very short. If you can dodge at the exact right moment and right direction (as it will do a mini charge if you just dash straight away from it) it will miss but if your dodge is on cooldown then you have to hope you're fast enough to move to the side in the small window. · "Krabaroo" gets bullied more often than not. Only issue I have with him is at times his jump and slam attacks visual damage zone seems to be smaller than the actual damage zone, but that could just be bad positioning luck. · "Krabken" can overwhelm you with all his allies being spawned making movement difficult (see first normal enemy point below) while at the same making it extremely difficult to actually see where you are if you end up beside or behind him unless you have gone for a plus size build. Add on the Tentacles he spawns and the meteors that spawn faster and faster and it becomes a visual nightmare. Also, the allies he spawns have all their attacks available to them; so, you can get stun-locked by Spiderfrogs or Spitfish++ traps in the middle of the boss fight and be promptly, unceremoniously, killed. For a boss fight where the player needs to keep moving to survive even more than others there are far too many ways your movement is specifically prevented. · "Shellephant" requires you to kite her around a tree in order to not get hit by her roll, you can ~at times~ time a dodge perfectly to avoid it. The trunk attack, which swings twice, is also most likely to hit you at least once. As, if you have to dodge the first, chances are the second ~will~ hit you and vice versa. So, the overall boss fight is just kiting her around a tree if you don't want to die, or if you're lucky you gained enough speed to be able to avoid her without it, ex she was your third boss and you have wings + legs, wings + slither/tentacles, or slither + tentacles. Addressing Normal Enemies: · All enemies (bosses included) can block & prevent your movement. Dodging can sometimes get you through, but it depends on the dodge type and pure luck. But enemies can push past you and push you around (in the literal sense). While you cannot do the same back. · "Beewares" can overwhelm you if you're on any terrain other than grass if you have no speed upgrades. It's technically possible to circle kite them on other terrains before speed upgrades but the majority of the success rate is luck on their attack timing. · "Blobfish". Poor Blobfish, they could use another prey counterpart that gets bullied too. They're all alone right now since HatBirbs just hide forever & get allies and SnowHares run away at lightning speed. · "Crabbybara" are hypocrites. · "HatBirbs" can stay in burrows forever. Which means, not only do they become immune from all harm, but they also prevent you from using an otherwise functional burrow forever. Unless they deign to come out of the burrow because sometimes, they feel like it or they're hungry, but don't hold your breath. · "Pantthers" will aggro on you before anything else and rush you, sometimes 3+ at a time. Just beat a difficult boss and survived by the skin of your teeth? Have 3 Pantther++'s running straight at you from 3 different directions past every other newly spawned animal, while the other animals around them aggro to each other as well as they should. Also, their speed is broken, I don't know what "Super Legendary" version of the "Sprint" Dash they have on top of there already high move speed but they're impossible to catch 90% of the time once fleeing, making fighting them & their alpha versions pointless and incredibly deadly unless you can kill them before they decide to turn into The Flash & never be seen again. For such a high damage dealing and fast enemy they have far too much health, it is as if they were meant to be glass cannons, but the developers decided to give them strong health anyway. Also, no, making them un-willing to go into water doesn't negate any of their BS. · "Pilferrets" can hide in burrows for a hilariously long time "eating" a piece of food they grab and run away with. They seem to be immune to damage as soon as they start the "enter the burrow" animation. Meaning, if you had one more hit to kill them and they get to the burrow you are better off forgetting about that Pilferret in most cases. · "SandSharks" attack damage zones are hard to see against the sand biome (hope this isn't how I find out I'm colour-blind lol) and their attacks happen too a bit too quick to be avoidable in my experience; if you are in the attack damage zone when it appears chances are you're taking that damage. Though, part or much of that could be caused by the aforementioned visibility difficulties. · "SnowHares" are also impossible to catch unless you can one-shot them, making their existence in the game almost pointless as you'll rarely interact with them. They do give a decent ally bonus (if you can get them) at least. · "Spineapple" are adorable. · "Spitfish", specifically the + & ++ varieties', headbutt attack can be hard to avoid but it's not as bad as the Sandshark for comparison ~as the attacks seem to function similar~. The Spear Stab/Swipe attack of the ++ variety is extremely annoying to try and avoid though and its speed doesn't help. They seem to also be able to lay traps that stun you, I am unclear on how to spot them visually. Which at the game-stage they appear it can be particularly frustrating if not, at a minimum, rude; especially during the Krabken boss fight. · "SpiderFrogs" tongue attack stuns you, this is only really bad during the Krabken boss fight where he can spawn multiple as allies, thereby potentially stun-locking you. I would also like their tongue attack as an attack option for the player; the closest we get is "Spit" but it's a different move shared with Spitfish & Aquaconda and lacks the stun functionality. Continued, 1 of Many (comments)

I do find the game after a few hours in to become quite same-y and I found myself putting on a show in the back as I went through more challenges but I didn't totally mind it. I like a good game where I don't feel like I need to restart the game if it's been a while since I played and this a perfect turn your brain off and relax, show on the tv laying on the couch kind of game. I know for others the samey-ness can be a turn off but I feel like Everything Is Crab kind of designed itself around that. You can find plenty of criticisms from other people about how the game progression feels broken, some evolutions aren't good or get power-crept out of viability, but, again, all of those things were why this game felt like it was in an optimistic early access stage. I cannot recommend a game that feels like it should go back to calling itself a beta product. It feels unfinished and like it needs a lot more playtesting to catch the weird glitches and bugs that are also regular occurrences. As for why I like the game, my reasons are all subjective (cute art, etc). The irony is that I WOULD recommend this game and give it a positive review--if, it had been in early access still...

I have noticed a number of dissenting comments to reviews that aren't glowing and they appear to come from either from people who love the game beyond reason or have an incentive to publicly attack fair criticism to the game. No person is obligated to play through and unlock the entire game before posting their review - 4 hours should be enough time to get a reasonable perspective of the game. If not, then the developers failed to demonstrate the range of the game until well after the refund period has expired. I am considerably concerned by the developers immediately pointing to paid DLC on a game that is mechanically incomplete and had just immediately launched. I really enjoyed the concept of the game shown through the demo and decided to make the buy - had I known that the demo represented close to the full depth of the game I would not have purchased it. I enjoy it for a quick ~15 minutes here and there because of its cute animations and bright sounds, but I am also put off on the lack of viability of multiple builds. This game, like many others seeks to financially capitalize on roguelikes and throws volume of mod options at you to distract from a lack of tuning instead of taking the time to hone mechanic design and diversity of content. This game isn't irredeemable, but it does need work if it isn't intended to be another quickly forgotten cash grab.
